subject.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly

question: Should configured Azure endpoint and model surfaces override the OpenAI manifest alias owner for normal deployments while unconditional OpenAI model suppressions still win, and should that rule live in the generic manifest resolver on current main?
rationale: The patch is coherent and proven, but it establishes a cross-provider authentication and transport ownership rule where current architecture also offers provider-owned normalization and suppression hooks; automation cannot safely choose the permanent owner boundary.

options.title: Confirm refreshed generic rule
options.body: Refresh onto current main, repeat the focused suite and probe, and approve the generic manifest resolver as the canonical ownership layer.

options.title: Move policy into provider
options.body: Keep core alias handling generic and implement Azure/OpenAI-specific ownership and suppression through existing provider hooks with equivalent coverage.

options.title: Pause for contract design
options.body: Keep the PR open until the provider-alias contract and overlapping core/plugin normalization paths are reconciled.

recommendation.title: Confirm refreshed generic rule
recommendation.body: Refresh onto current main, repeat the focused suite and probe, and approve the generic manifest resolver as the canonical ownership layer.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work most directly owns the OpenAI/Codex provider catalog, dynamic resolver, manifest rows, and suppression behavior involved in this decision.
